basis: R1485 preserves 3-5 percent PE gains but still changes old scalar/SIMD layout and native performance. R1489 rules out increased SIMD instruction work and identifies increased branch misses. Source inspection also shows new C6/C7 ModR/M bounds/group checks in the shared iterator before the memory reader loads the same byte again.
change: Transfer only C6/C7 ModR/M bounds and memory-/group-zero admission to the constant-specialized immediate-memory reader, sharing its one ModR/M load. Leave old memory opcode admission in the iterator and preserve the tagged plan table exactly.
distinct_from: R1483 moved existing memory-family opcode classification into the memory reader and increased old-path work. This experiment moves only the newly admitted immediate-store check and changes no old opcode policy.
hypothesis: A smaller common dispatch body and removal of duplicate new-path ModR/M reads may preserve PE gains with fewer effects on old output paths. Native sampling does not yet prove this fixes the branch-miss mechanism.
validation: Seven units, generated-table identity, canonical projection checks, baseline full-record and guard-page comparison, and exact R1485 admission census before cross-host cost and timing qualification.
